newsitem.title: DUBAI: GOLF-UNDERDOG GREEN SURPRISES NORMAN AND WOOSNAM.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-UNDERDOG GREEN SURPRISES NORMAN AND WOOSNAM.

text.p: Australian underdog Richard Green sank a 12-foot playoff putt against Ian Woosnam and Greg Norman to win the Dubai Desert Classic after Woosnam had thrown it away on Sunday.

The 26-year-old from Melbourne, ranked 198th in the world, made his winning birdie on the first extra hole, the 17th, after sinking a curling 20-footer for birdie from the fringe of the green at the last hole of the final round to earn his playoff chance.
His victory over a strong field made him the first left-hander to win a European Tour event since New Zealander Bob Charles took the Swiss Open in 1974.
But Woosnam, bidding for a special 39th birthday present, threw it away on a muffed pitch shot at the 72nd hole with the winner's cheque of 116,660 pounds ($189,000) all but in his pocket.
Woosnam needed a par five to take the title and played safe by laying up with his second shot short of the lake that guards the 18th green.
But he mishit his pitch from 80 yards and it landed on the bank of the green and bounced back into the lake.
"It was a poor shot. I actually felt I hit it all right but I must have caught it heavy," Woosnam said.

He salvaged his chances by holing from 12 feet for a bogey six to get into the playoff. Norman, who had birdied the last from eight feet, shot a final round of 66, Green 68 and Woosnam 69 for 16-under-par aggregates of 272.

"To win this tournament against those guys is absolutely unbelievable. I'm just buzzing. What a fantastic last couple of putts to make," said Green, who is in his first full year on the European Tour.
"The putt on the 18th was something special really, just to get into the playoff. The whole moment was pretty special.
"If you're going to get involved in a playoff, you might as well make it against Norman and Woosnam."
Spain's Jose Maria Olazabal completed a fine return from his 18 months break because of crippling foot problems by shooting a 71 for a nine-under-par total of 279 and a share of 12th place.
Bernhard Langer held fourth place on his own after a closing 69, the German losing his chance with a bogey six at the long 15th after leaving his second shot in the rough and then fluffing a chip.
Fellow German Thomas Goegele grabbed fifth place with a six- under 66 for a 13-under total of 275, but European number one Colin Montgomerie never mounted a challenge.
Two shots behind overnight, he came to grief at the huge lake that fronts the ninth and 18th greens and which he cleared so dramatically with his second shot at the last when he won last year.
This time he hit into it at the ninth on the way to a double bogey six and again at 18 for a bogey six as he compiled a 71.
He shared sixth place on 276 with Briton Malcolm Mackenzie and Irishman Paul McGinley, who shot 70 and 69 respectively.

Green, who made his decision to become an affiliate European Tour member after placing fifth in last year's Heineken Classic in Perth -- level with American John Daly -- said that when Woosnam drove to the left side at the last hole he realised the Welshman could not go for the green.
Green knew that if he got on the green in two "anything could happen." Although he finished on the fringe, he holed with a magnificent putt to get into the playoff.
Green, whose caddy is his wife Anita, had to wait while Norman and Woosnam both putted from the fringe at the playoff 17th, both missing to the left side.
But his approach had finished in the middle of the green. "I had 89 yards to the front and 106 to the pin. I hit a sand iron at three-quarter pace with spin on it," he said.
"All I could feel was my heart pumping."
Green began here with rounds of 70 and 68 but climbed into contention with a 66 on Saturday.
Norman, playing his first full tournamnent after a three- month break, said he was pleased at his decision to play here in advance of next week's Doral Open in Florida.
"I played well and I was glad to get into the playoff. I am glad I came over here," he said. "Richard played great. I have now played one hole with him so that is him one up on me."
